name: Gamuda Berhad
oneLine: A builder of large infrastructure such as rail lines, tunnels, dams and data centres, which also develops housing townships.
inPlainWords: Gamuda does two main things. First, governments and large clients pay it to build big projects: metro and rail lines, tunnels, expressways, water treatment plants, dams, renewable energy plants and data centres.
Second, it buys land and builds townships and buildings, then sells the homes and commercial units.
It was founded in 1976 and now works in nine countries. In 2025 most of its revenue came from outside Malaysia, with Australia the largest market.

flow.label: Wins contracts
flow.detail: Bids for infrastructure projects from governments and large clients. Work already won but not yet built: more than RM38 billion.

flow.label: Builds over several years
flow.detail: Earns revenue as each project progresses, so a contract won today pays out over years.

flow.label: Develops land
flow.detail: Buys land, builds townships and sells homes. Homes sold but not yet billed: RM8 billion.

flow.label: Profit
flow.detail: Construction brought 61% of pre-tax profit in 2025 and property 39% (calculated from the segment figures).

moneyNote: Construction gives most of the revenue, but property is more profitable per ringgit: it made 23% of revenue and 39% of pre-tax profit (calculated from the segment figures).
